reason: I want to prepare the flight carrier at the cold transfer bench so the discovery can be moved into it.
expectation: I expect the carrier to be prepared for a cold transfer, though I don't know exactly what the bench will do.

alternatives.reason: Placing the discovery case at the bench also seems necessary, but I chose to prepare the receiving carrier first.

effect: The carrier and its transfer buffer are now chilled, so the full body-bearing core can be moved into a prepared cradle.
reaction: It's reassuring that the surrounding ice has room to travel with the specimen.
reason: Combining the discovery case with the conditioned carrier at the cold bench directly advances the transfer goal.
expectation: I expect the core and neighboring ice to be transferred into the chilled flight carrier while remaining cold, though the exact procedure is unclear.

effect: The sealed core and its neighboring ice are now together in the flight carrier, ready for the lander.
reaction: It's satisfying that the whole preserved layer made the transfer intact.
reason: The only offered combination places the packed core in the refrigerated sample bay, directly advancing the goal.
expectation: I expect the carrier to be secured in the lander's refrigerated bay and the transfer goal to be completed.

effect: The carrier is locked into the lander's bay and connected to powered cooling, completing the transfer of the core and its surrounding ice.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the thermal buffer bridge the transfer and the refrigerator take over.

mostWorthwhile.text: Transferring the sealed liner into the conditioned carrier was most worthwhile: the body-bearing core and neighboring ice stayed together, preserving the layer around the discovery.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the packed core in the refrigerated bay felt predictable because it was the only combination offered, though it completed the transfer.

surprise.text: I learned that the flight carrier had a thermal buffer to bridge the transfer before powered cooling took over.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each had a clear role in preparing, packing, or cooling the core.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what the receiving laboratory learns from the intact core and its surrounding ice.
